problem_text: The Global Network Infrastructure Initiative is upgrading its telecommunications grid across 100 regional sectors. To comply with the hardware allocation budget set for the upcoming fiscal decade, the engineering board has authorized the activation of exactly 10 sectors to serve as Primary Uplink Nodes. Each sector functions under a specific routing protocol defined in the `chains` registry. This registry dictates a rigid priority sequence of potential Uplink Nodes for every sector acting as a data origin. When a sector initiates a data transmission, the network protocol scans its assigned priority sequence in ascending order and connects to the first sector that has been activated as a Primary Uplink Node. The system efficiency metric, known as the Transmission Lag Index, is calculated for each sector as the zero-based ordinal position of the connected Uplink Node within that sector's specific priority chain. Additionally, sectors with identification numbers divisible by 4 contain legacy copper infrastructure requiring distinct maintenance schedules compared to the fiber-optic cables in odd-numbered sectors, which have a signal attenuation rate of 0.05dB per kilometer. Any sector not chosen as a Primary Uplink Node will revert to a passive relay state, consuming 15% of the standard energy output to maintain heartbeat signals. The objective is to identify the optimal set of Uplink Nodes to minimize the total Transmission Lag Index across all sectors.
